I call myself a software developer because 99% of the time I'm working on a system that has no sure target.  I cannot design or engineer myself to the solution because no one knows what it looks like.  The only way to find the target is to iteratively build it and see what people think.  Refactoring, YAGNI, and a boyscout rule to code quality is critical here.

I view software engineering as something a bit 'harder' in the science sense.  You have a hard target with hard requirements and you should be using methods to hit those targets. You can spend a bit more time on design here because you're more sure of what you're building.

Both types of programming have processes.  You can't do the first without an iterative process.  And I believe the best way to do the 2nd is with an iterative process because that's the best way to confirm what you've built matches what was envisioned.
